elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B retains "M&I shall indemnify Customer from, and defend Customer against," and "Customer" is defined as "Tri City National Bank ... (including its Affiliates, 'Customer')"; new Paragraph C also states the "indemnity and defense obligations under Paragraph B shall also run to Customer's affiliates." Duty to defend and affiliate coverage are both present (the Paragraph C affiliate extension is redundant of the definition).

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B(i)-(ii) expressly cover "any claim by a third party", and the indemnity runs to "Customer", a term that already includes its Affiliates; Paragraph C confirms the extension to affiliates. Section 14.3 also frames the mechanic around "any third party [that] makes a claim covered by this Section".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Retained Paragraph B(i): "any claim by a third party that the Services or M&I's software infringe upon any United States patent, copyright or trademark of a third party." Note the narrowness (US patent/copyright/trademark only; no trade-secret misappropriation or non-US rights) — a sub-element shortfall to record in the rationale, not a failure of the element.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New Paragraph C(i): indemnity/defense "shall further extend to any liability or expenses arising out of or relating to (i) M&I's violation of applicable law", curing the pre-existing limitation to protected-class laws in B(iv).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New Paragraph C(ii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer's data caused by M&I" — Vendor-caused and covering data of Customer (including, via the definition, its Affiliates).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: New Paragraph C(iii): "M&I's gross negligence or wilful misconduct" — both categories expressly named.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 (unchanged): "such indemnitee shall give notice of such claim to the indemnifying party, including a brief description of the amount and basis therefor, if known."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 (unchanged): the indemnifying party "shall be entitled to assume control of the defense of the claim with counsel chosen by the indemnifying party, reasonably satisfactory to the indemnitee."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 (unchanged): "Indemnitee shall cooperate fully with, and assist, the indemnifying party in its defense against such claim in all reasonable respects."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Paragraph A as rendered: "(i) content, data, or materials provided by Customer to M&I and (ii) Customer's violation of applicable law"; the former representations/protected-class/harassment/injury/property-loss and Section 6.6(B) limbs are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B(i) covers third-party claims that the Services or M&I's software infringe US patent, copyright or trademark rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification exclusion is imposed, and none is required; the condition does not bite because the indemnity contains no such carve-out.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion appears and none is needed, so the element is not offended.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification exclusion appears, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Neither Paragraph B, new Paragraph C nor Section 14.3 contains any procure/modify/replace remedy for infringement; no such language was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-on-failure-of-remedies mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is proposed; the rationale expressly declines to pursue it, and retained Section 13.4 caps M&I liability at three months' payments instead.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the three missing conduct limbs (breach of applicable law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access/disclosure of Customer data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) are added in operative Paragraph C, the retained Paragraph B supplies the IP limb and duty to defend, Section 14.3 supplies notice/control/cooperation, and Paragraph A is narrowed to Customer-supplied content and Customer's violation of law.

Minimality fails on duplicate coverage: "Customer" is defined in the preamble as "Tri City National Bank ... (including its Affiliates, 'Customer')", so Paragraph B's indemnity and defense already run to Customer's affiliates. Delete the words "shall also run to Customer's affiliates, and" from Paragraph C and open it as "M&I's indemnity and defense obligations under Paragraph B shall further extend to ..."; the affiliate element is met by the definition alone.

Secondary drafting point (not an element failure): Paragraph C uses lowercase "affiliates" and "Customer's data" rather than the agreement's defined "Affiliates"/Customer Data terminology; if the affiliate limb is retained at all, conform the capitalisation to avoid an undefined-term argument.

Intent is preserved: the IP limb, the third-party-services limb, the enforcement-cost recovery in both paragraphs, and the whole of Section 14.3 survive unchanged, and no cross-reference is left dangling by the edits. One check for the drafter: confirm Section 6.6(B) does not itself point back to Section 14.2(A)(vi), so that dropping that limb from Paragraph A leaves no orphaned reference in Section 6.6(B).

Fallback level is not complete (no procure/modify/replace remedy, no refund fallback, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is met; record in the rationale that the retained IP indemnity reaches only United States patent, copyright and trademark claims and does not cover trade-secret misappropriation or non-US rights.
